record.name: Commodity Supplemental Food Program (CSFP)
record.administeredBy: U.S. Department of Agriculture, administered by the Wisconsin Department of Health Services; distributed by community action agencies and food banks (Community Action Coalition of South Central Wisconsin serves Dane County)
record.summary: A monthly box of USDA foods for Wisconsin residents 60 or older with limited income. Sometimes called Stockbox or Cupboard Bound locally.
record.benefit: A monthly food package: fruits and juice, vegetables, cheese, milk, meat/poultry/fish, plant-based proteins, cereals, pasta, and rice, plus nutrition education.

steps: Find the CSFP agency that serves your county (Dane County: Community Action Coalition of South Central Wisconsin, 4101 E Towne Blvd., Madison).
Contact that agency to enroll; you may be placed on a waiting list.
Pick up your food box monthly at the distribution site.

record._statusNote: 'Agencies may have waiting lists' -- stated on the page. Modelled as waitlist rather than open.

of._sourceText: Be aged 60 or older. (Our AGE_BANDS: under-60 / 60-64 / 65-plus. '60 or older' = the last two bands -- expressible, unlike the WWWP 40-64 case.)

Make a certain amount of money (review table on this page). [OR] Wisconsin allows for automatic CSFP eligibility, regardless of income, for current participation in one of these federal programs: SNAP/FoodShare, FDPIR, SSI, Low Income Subsidy Program, Medicare Savings Programs.

based on 150% of the ... 2026 Poverty Guidelines ... use total gross income (before taxes and deductions) of all household members. Table: household size 1 = $1,995/month, +$710 per additional member.

of._note: Source also lists FDPIR, Low Income Subsidy Program, and Medicare Savings Programs as categorical routes -- none of those are options in the currentBenefits fact today.

rule._factsNote: Fully expressible with existing facts (state, age, annualHouseholdIncome+householdSize via incomeAtOrBelow, currentBenefits) EXCEPT the three categorical programs (FDPIR, Low Income Subsidy, Medicare Savings) that are not in BENEFIT_ENROLLMENTS. Adding them is a vocabulary question, not a schema one.
unencodable: Categorical eligibility via FDPIR, the Medicare Part D Low Income Subsidy (Extra Help), or a Medicare Savings Program -- routes not in the currentBenefits vocabulary.
The income figure is monthly gross; incomeAtOrBelow() consumes an annual figure, so a faithful encoding needs the annual equivalent of the published monthly table (or the % works directly).

hops: nutrition/csfp.htm 'Do I qualify?' section carries the full rule inline, including the size-scoped income table

scopeColocated.scopeLocation: The renderStructured output keeps the column headers attached ('Household size = 1 | Monthly income = $1,995'), and the two scope notes -- '150% of the 2026 Poverty Guidelines' and 'use total gross income of all household members' -- sit in the paragraph immediately above the table. This is the well-behaved case: table + headers + scope note all within a screen.

Stated directly above the table. Search snippets for this program returned '150 percent' AND older third-party pages saying '130 percent'; the fetched primary page settles it at 150%. (Historically CSFP was 130% FPL -- do not carry that forward.)

cost.notes: 1 fetch + 1 search. The search result and an old third-party PDF disagreed on the % FPL (130 vs 150); fetching dhs.wisconsin.gov/nutrition/csfp.htm directly resolved it to 150% as of Feb 2026.

surprises: A textbook well-formed source: clean table, headers, scope note, categorical branch all colocated. It is a useful negative control for the pilot -- proof that not every source fights back, and that the scopeColocated field can register a clean 'yes' and mean it.
